reading: A microreactor priced at the published $200–330/MWh range beats remote diesel ($250–400/MWh) and beats rural Alaska ($350–600/MWh) outright — but loses badly to grid-connected U.S. industrial power. The PTC and at-scale cases ($35–90/MWh) are the only ones that reach grid parity, and both are forward-looking. The commercial logic therefore inverts by sector: off-grid sites buy on cost today; on-grid sites buy on resilience, speed-to-power or carbon, and pay a premium to do it.
